summary: A projection divergence is recorded once as a P1 bug with what a reproduction needs, and never repaired; the check is off by default and at most hourly

replay.detail: No replay changes. Nothing replays or repairs a divergent projection.

schema.detail: No table, column, index or schema version changes. The claim registry adds an optional reproduction object field to operational.failure (docs/st3/schema.md regenerated). Divergence faults are operational.failure and operational.recovered claims, kinds that already exist, on daemon/NODE subjects, a family those kinds already accept.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, admission, retention or drop-rule changes.

compatibility.detail: Replication exchanges carry an optional build field, the sender's build revision, skipped when absent; older peers ignore it and leave it out, and a divergence with such a peer records its build as unknown. operational.failure gains an optional reproduction object field in the claim registry; members on older builds keep it as an unknown field without enforcing it, like any closed-schema field added later. Divergence faults carry it (projection, members, inventory_digest, writer_high_water, digests, builds, since_unix_ms, compared_at_unix_ms); readers that do not know it ignore it. slo/targets.toml gains a [divergence] table (max_open = 0); the file is built into each daemon, so no running config changes. On a daemon that runs the check, GET /v1/slo gains a projection-divergence objective row and st doctor a slo/projection-divergence line, both from the count the last check read.

manual.detail: The divergence check is off unless the daemon's environment sets ST3_DIVERGENCE_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS (milliseconds; under an hour means hourly; unset or zero means off). It is an environment variable, not a config key, so rolling back to an older build needs no config edit.

recovery.detail: With the check on, a divergence that outlasts the projection delay opens one high-priority fault for the fleet's fault agent on the recording member's daemon/NODE subject, one per member pair and projection, and it ends when the latest comparison with that peer at the same envelopes finds the whole graph equal. Comparisons are held in memory, so a restart leaves an open fault open until the next comparison that agrees. The check runs at most hourly, reads comparisons in memory and, with one indexed read, every operational failure and recovery ever recorded on the compared daemon subjects, keeping the divergence ones, so its cost grows with that history; skips while the writer or write transactions ran over target in the last minute or replication is catching up, and writes only to open or end a fault.
